purpose: Advisory comparison of nine discovery candidates with reviewer-chosen shortlists of the nearest prior catalog patterns.

C1.title: Confidence gate adjusted for Choice option count
C1.mechanism: Code converts a confidence threshold into the top-probability it implies for each option count (confidence = (n*p_max-1)/(n-1)), versions thresholds with the option set, and checks stored confidence against probabilities, because a flat threshold demands different top probabilities as options are added or removed.

C2.title: Tool-call trace audit split between code and Jev
C2.mechanism: Code validates call/result ID binding, argument schema conformance, and exact value equality between request fields, arguments and earlier tool outputs; Jev judges only whether each tool suits the request and whether a free-text argument refers to the requested entity.

C3.title: Compound-request split and re-ask
C3.mechanism: A Noul detects a request containing several distinct actions; an LLM splits it into atomic commands; code caps the split count; Jev checks that the commands jointly cover the request and add nothing; each command is then re-evaluated with the ordinary routing questions before any execution.

C4.title: Email phishing signal profile with veto
C4.mechanism: Separate Nouls for credential request, unexpected reward, time pressure, display-name organization claim and link-text destination claim, while code parses sender and link domains; a credential request is a veto to quarantine instead of one term in a weighted average.

C5.title: Language-aware confidence gate
C5.mechanism: Code detects the input language before inference; non-English inputs receive stricter thresholds, a human-review route, or a translate-then-ask path with the translation kept as provenance, because the provider states English accuracy is best.

C6.title: Model-alias movement canary
C6.mechanism: Code records the versioned model ID returned with every answer; when a floating alias resolves to a new version, threshold-gated automation is held and the frozen fixture set is rerun before thresholds are re-qualified.

C7.title: Reasoning-model ensemble label bootstrap
C7.mechanism: When no labels exist, several reasoning models label a sample; code keeps only agreed labels with provenance, measures label noise on a small human-labelled holdout, then trains a classical model on Jev probability features.

C8.title: Two-budget question packer
C8.mechanism: Code packs speculative questions into requests under two provider limits, total state plus all questions and state plus the single longest question, splitting batches deterministically and recording the limit version.

C9.title: Question/negation pair ambiguity probe
C9.mechanism: At design time only, the same proposition and its literal negation are asked as two Nouls; a large deviation of their sum from one flags the wording for literal rewrite, never as a runtime correctness signal.

H11.title: Confidence-backed taxonomy traversal with broad fallback
H11.purpose: Return the best supported category without forcing a brittle leaf when the current node is uncertain.

H20.title: Human-adjudication confidence ledger
H20.purpose: Track whether a predeclared low-stakes Noul policy is calibrated enough for its chosen review threshold on later human-labeled cases.

H32.title: Choice plurality, agreement, and abstention audit
H32.purpose: Expose the operational tradeoff between repeat agreement and confidence-based abstention for a Choice workflow.

H12.title: Repeated-decision stability gate
H12.purpose: Measure whether the same bounded low-stakes judgment remains stable across a small fixed sample before auto-suggesting a route.

H06.title: Keep illustrative values out of real tool arguments
H06.purpose: Catch an LLM copying a sample path or record value from documentation into a real operation.

L04.title: Select an available tool handler
L04.purpose: Keep simple calculations and lookups out of a large reasoning call while respecting actual tool availability.

E25.title: Classify trace-event relationship type
E25.purpose: Separate causality evidence from same-request and merely temporal log correlation.

E23.title: Verify cross-field label/value associations
E23.purpose: Catch a structured output whose values appear in source text but are paired to the wrong labels.

B01.title: Route the current business request
B01.purpose: Reduce transfers between billing, service and estimating queues.

L19.title: Classify answer work type before model routing
L19.purpose: Pick a response workflow based on the requested work shape rather than treating all questions as free-form generation.

H28.title: Bounded speculative fan-out scheduler
H28.purpose: Batch independent work while preventing stale or inapplicable speculative branches from driving an action.

L05.title: Choose the clarification that unlocks a useful answer
L05.purpose: Convert vague LLM requests into a specific target, success condition and compatible constraint set.

H36.title: Ingress/egress message-risk ledger
H36.purpose: Keep independently screened input and output risks separate so code can apply phase-specific policy.

H19.title: Policy hazard/severity routing matrix
H19.purpose: Combine independently judged policy-hazard presence and described consequence severity into a caller-owned review route.

H24.title: Atomic score composition with veto policy
H24.purpose: Keep semantic dimensions reusable while code decides which preferences may compensate and which failures must veto.

L21.title: Classify retrieved-content instruction posture
L21.purpose: Flag behavior-directing text inside retrieved material without converting that classification into an injection-safety guarantee.

L08.title: Classify input text role before prompt assembly
L08.purpose: Keep task requests, binding constraints, reference material and quoted third-party instructions distinguishable.

L19.title: Classify answer work type before model routing
L19.purpose: Pick a response workflow based on the requested work shape rather than treating all questions as free-form generation.

H40.title: Semantic-feature drift and retraining hold
H40.purpose: Stop a semantic-feature pipeline from silently reusing an old evaluation after question, population, or held-out behavior changes.

H21.title: Pin a decision response to the source snapshot
H21.purpose: Reject a semantically plausible typed result when code cannot bind it to the current source snapshot.

H35.title: Semantic lint canary and human-disagreement controller
H35.purpose: Admit a semantic lint change only after a fixed labeled canary exposes new disagreements for review.

H16.title: Pending-action invalidation on material state change
H16.purpose: Reconsider an unexecuted proposed action when fresh evidence invalidates a stated precondition or changes its target.

H38.title: Feature-matrix provenance and holdout challenger
H38.purpose: Make semantic-feature revisions and held-out evidence bindings inspectable while deterministic code owns metric comparison.

L24.title: Classify semantic feature-question validity
L24.purpose: Reject feature questions that leak the target, duplicate existing signals, or cannot be observed from permitted text.

H04.title: Route reviewer disagreement by what would resolve it
H04.purpose: Avoid majority voting when reviewers are judging different facts, subjects or preferences.

H22.title: Candidate-universe coverage gate
H22.purpose: Keep a Choice winner from becoming a real-world selection unless the candidate universe is declared adequate.

H31.title: Noul threshold-crossing repeat audit
H31.purpose: Keep repeated probability samples visible when a policy threshold could change a disposition.

H05.title: Repair the demonstrated question defect, not the whole prompt
H05.purpose: Turn a failed Jev judgment into a bounded, auditable repair target.

L23.title: Classify primitive or composition fit
L23.purpose: Choose an output type that matches the desired JSON consumer before writing a brittle prompt-and-parse contract.

host_review.method: Each flagged overlap was checked against the prior pattern's value, comparison, code ownership and question text. Where host judgment differs from Jev, both are recorded.

C1.note: H32 audits Choice agreement across repeats; none converts thresholds by option count.

C2.note: Host disagrees in part: E23 judges field pairing inside one assembled record against a source document. C2's delta is the code/Jev partition over a multi-call trace, with code owning ID binding and cross-call value flow. Its Jev questions reuse L04 and E23, so priority is lowered.

C3.note: H28 batches independent questions; it does not split a compound request or check split coverage.

C4.note: Accepted: the veto composition is H24. Only the phishing question set is new, as an email-domain profile citing H24.

C5.note: No prior pattern gates on input language.

C6.note: Accepted: re-admission after change is H35/H40. The new element is using a changed resolved model version as the trigger, recorded in kernel evaluation guidance.

C7.note: H38 binds feature provenance and holdout; it does not produce labels from a reasoning-model ensemble.

C8.note: Accepted on host review: H28 already owns stated budgets. The two provider limits are a concrete H28 parameterization.

C9.note: The provider page warns the pair need not sum to one; use only as a design-time wording prompt after validation.

boundary: A bounded shortlist comparison, not a global prior-art or novelty search. Shortlists were chosen by the host; Jev cannot find a closer pattern omitted from them. Answers are advisory and were checked by reading the prior patterns.
